title: Bidirectional BFS in Zürich: Find the shortest route!
description: Watch Bidirectional BFS race from both the start and goal on a real street-map style graph. It meets in the middle, often shrinking search time compared to one-direction BFS.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ Zürich (Seefeld) meets graph theory—let’s watch **Bidirectional BFS** ignite! 

🚦 **How it works (the nerdy magic):** we run BFS from **Start** and **Goal** simultaneously, each expanding level-by-level in an unweighted graph. When the two frontiers intersect, the combined path is guaranteed to be **shortest** (minimum number of edges), because BFS explores in waves of equal distance. 

🗺️ **Why it’s perfect for street maps:** treating real intersections/blocks as nodes and street segments as edges turns navigation into an unweighted shortest-path search. Bidirectional BFS effectively halves the “distance horizon” in many practical layouts—so the visualization shows fewer explored nodes before the meet point lights up. 

💡 Want more pathfinding reels (A*, Dijkstra, BFS variants)? Like + follow, then comment what start/end streets you’d choose in **Zürich (Seefeld)**—I'll generate the next map! 🔥
fb_caption:

📌 Street maps become a graph: intersections = nodes, streets = edges. Share this reel with a friend who loves coding or algorithms, and tell us which neighborhood pairing you want next!
